title: Three-counit transpose of iterated proper product comparisons
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p_0,\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_{p_0^a}$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\geq1$. Choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, $n\geq1$, and a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] with the specified canonical transformations [def-exchange-projection, def-sf-pf]. All schemes and arrows below are separated and of finite type over $k$; all inputs lie in the displayed bounded constructible finite-Tor categories. Integral pullback and tensor are completed; field operations use rationalization and common finite coefficient fields. For any $u:U\to B$, $v:V\to B$ with projections $\pi_U,\pi_V$ on $U\times_BV$, write $u\times_Bv=u\pi_U=v\pi_V$, $P\boxtimes Q=L\pi_U^*P\otimes^L_\Lambda L\pi_V^*Q$, and define the specified morphism
$$\lambda_{u,v}(P,Q)=\alpha_{v,\pi_V}\circ Rv_!\bigl(\operatorname{PF}_{\pi_V,L\pi_U^*P,Q}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{u,v}(P)\otimes1_Q)\bigr)\circ\Psi_v(Ru_!P,Q),$$
where $\Psi_v(F,Q)=Rv_!(\sigma_{Q,Lv^*F})\circ\operatorname{PF}_{v,Q,F}\circ\sigma_{F,Rv_!Q}$ and $\alpha$ is the supplied compact-support compositor. Let $f:X\to B$, $g:Y\to B$, $h:W\to B$ be proper, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, $M\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$. Put $F=Rf_*K$, $G=Rg_*L$, $H=Rh_*M$, $t:X\times_BY\to B$, $z:Y\times_BW\to B$, $V=X\times_BY\times_BW$, and $v:V\to B$, with projections $r_X,r_Y,r_W,r_{XY},r_{YW}$. Use the canonical proper normalizations $Ru_!=Ru_*$ and adjunction-compatible composition comparisons. Define
$$\Theta_L=\lambda_{t,h}(K\boxtimes L,M)\circ(\lambda_{f,g}(K,L)\otimes1_H),\qquad
\Theta_R=\lambda_{f,z}(K,L\boxtimes M)\circ(1_F\otimes\lambda_{g,h}(L,M)).$$
After the canonical fibre-product and tensor associators, both have codomain $Rv_*(Lr_X^*K\otimes^LLr_Y^*L\otimes^LLr_W^*M)$. Their transposes under $Lv^*\dashv Rv_*$ are both exactly
$$Lv^*(F\otimes^LG\otimes^LH)\cong Lr_X^*Lf^*F\otimes^LLr_Y^*Lg^*G\otimes^LLr_W^*Lh^*H
\xrightarrow{Lr_X^*\varepsilon_f\otimes Lr_Y^*\varepsilon_g\otimes Lr_W^*\varepsilon_h}
Lr_X^*K\otimes^LLr_Y^*L\otimes^LLr_W^*M.$$
Here $\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_h$ are the ordinary adjunction counits and the tensor comparisons are the canonical signed symmetric monoidal pullback comparisons. In particular the assertion identifies the transposes of the specified composites, rather than choosing a new ternary product map.

proof.text: All projections from a binary fibre product are base changes of its two structure maps. Thus $t,z,v$, and the projections needed for their binary product squares, are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a),(b). The operations in [def-sf-datum] are functors on the displayed finite-Tor categories, so $A=K\boxtimes L$, $D=L\boxtimes M$, $F,G,H,t_*A,z_*D$ and the tensors below are in the required domains. Write $u^*=Lu^*$, $u_*=Ru_*$ and $\otimes=\otimes^L_\Lambda$ in the canonical proper coordinates of the statement. Set $C=r_X^*K\otimes r_Y^*L\otimes r_W^*M$, $a=\lambda_{f,g}(K,L)$ and $b=\lambda_{g,h}(L,M)$. For $e:N\to u_*P$ its adjunction transpose is $\partial_u(e)=\varepsilon_{u,P}\circ u^*e$. This is the counit description of the adjunction in (A1), not a choice of another map. Use the natural tensor-pullback comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] throughout, including their compatibility with pullback composition and tensor associativity.

source.place: Clause (ii), associativity of tensor with PF, and final two-counit sentence: returned steps 2--4, extracting the proper three-counit transpose computation.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-proper-product-counit-transpose] to $(f,g;K,L)$, $(g,h;L,M)$, $(t,h;A,M)$ and $(f,z;K,D)$. Its definition of $\lambda$ is exactly the exchange/PF/$\Psi$ composite in this statement, including the same proper normalization and adjunction-compatible compositor. If $p_X,p_Y:X\times_BY\to X,Y$ and $q_Y,q_W:Y\times_BW\to Y,W$ are the projections, its four equalities give, in the canonical tensor coordinates,
$$\partial_t(a)=p_X^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes p_Y^*\varepsilon_{g,L},\qquad
\partial_z(b)=q_Y^*\varepsilon_{g,L}\otimes q_W^*\varepsilon_{h,M},$$
$$\partial_v(\lambda_{t,h}(A,M))=r_{XY}^*\varepsilon_{t,A}\otimes r_W^*\varepsilon_{h,M},\qquad
\partial_v(\lambda_{f,z}(K,D))=r_X^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes r_{YW}^*\varepsilon_{z,D}.$$
Here the last two sources are respectively $v^*(t_*A\otimes H)$ and $v^*(F\otimes z_*D)$. They do not yet have the common source $v^*(F\otimes G\otimes H)$: the inner maps must still be inserted.

source.place: Clause (ii), associativity of tensor with PF, and final two-counit sentence: returned steps 2--4, extracting the proper three-counit transpose computation.

proof.text:
Compute the left iteration using the transpose definition and functoriality. Naturality of the tensor-pullback comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identifies $v^*(a\otimes1_H)$ with $r_{XY}^*t^*a\otimes1_{r_W^*h^*H}$. The third equality of Step 2 therefore yields
$$\begin{aligned}
\partial_v(\Theta_L)
&=(r_{XY}^*\varepsilon_{t,A}\otimes r_W^*\varepsilon_{h,M})\circ(r_{XY}^*t^*a\otimes1)\\
&=r_{XY}^*(\varepsilon_{t,A}\circ t^*a)\otimes r_W^*\varepsilon_{h,M}\\
&=r_{XY}^*(p_X^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes p_Y^*\varepsilon_{g,L})\otimes r_W^*\varepsilon_{h,M}\\
&=r_X^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes r_Y^*\varepsilon_{g,L}\otimes r_W^*\varepsilon_{h,M}.
\end{aligned}$$
The second line is bifunctoriality of tensor and functoriality of pullback; the third is the first binary equality of [lem-sf-proper-product-counit-transpose]. The last line uses $p_Xr_{XY}=r_X$, $p_Yr_{XY}=r_Y$ and the composition compatibility of the cited tensor-pullback comparisons. Its source is precisely the three-factor pullback of $F\otimes G\otimes H$ displayed in the statement and its target is $C$.

source.place: Clause (ii), associativity of tensor with PF, and final two-counit sentence: returned steps 2--4, extracting the proper three-counit transpose computation.

proof.text:
For the right iteration, naturality of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identifies $v^*(1_F\otimes b)$ with $1_{r_X^*f^*F}\otimes r_{YW}^*z^*b$. The fourth equality of Step 2 and the second binary equality of [lem-sf-proper-product-counit-transpose] give
$$\begin{aligned}
\partial_v(\Theta_R)
&=(r_X^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes r_{YW}^*\varepsilon_{z,D})\circ(1\otimes r_{YW}^*z^*b)\\
&=r_X^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes r_{YW}^*(\varepsilon_{z,D}\circ z^*b)\\
&=r_X^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes r_{YW}^*(q_Y^*\varepsilon_{g,L}\otimes q_W^*\varepsilon_{h,M})\\
&=r_X^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes r_Y^*\varepsilon_{g,L}\otimes r_W^*\varepsilon_{h,M}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality uses $q_Yr_{YW}=r_Y$, $q_Wr_{YW}=r_W$ and tensor-pullback composition compatibility. Associativity compatibility in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identifies this source and target with those of Step 3. Hence both transposes are exactly the specified map. No factor is permuted in these calculations; the signed symmetries inside each $\lambda$ were already accounted for by the binary lemma. That lemma and the tensor-pullback comparisons apply at all four coefficient stages, so the calculation also uses completed integral operations and the supplied rational/common-stage operations directly, without inferring equality of integral maps from finite reductions.
